133
RAJYA  SABHA
————
List of Questions for ORAL ANSWERS
to be asked at a sitting of the Rajya Sabha to be held on
Tuesday, September 6, 2011/Bhadra 15, 1933 (Saka)
————
(Ministries : Drinking Water and Sanitation; Environment and Forests;
Finance; Health and Family Welfare; Heavy Industries and Public
Enterprises;Petroleum and Natural Gas; Rural Development)
Total number of questions — 20
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
Non-availability of cheap vaccines
*461. DR E. M. SUDARSANA
NATCHIAPPAN: Will the Minister of
HEALTH AND FAMILY WELFARE be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has ordered
suspension of manufacturing licences of
three PSUs namely, Central Research
Institute at Kasauli, Pasteur Institute of
India at Coonoor and BCG Vaccine
Laboratory at Chennai in January, 2008;
and
(b) if so, whether their closure has
coincided with non-availability of vaccines
for the poor people and increase of cost of
vaccines by 50-70 per cent by private sector?
Difficulties faced by forest officers
*462. SHRI PYARIMOHAN
MOHAPATRA: Will the Minister of
ENVIRONMENT AND FORESTS be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
difficulties faced by forest officers in the
field due to conflicting provisions of the
Forest Rights Act, the Forest Conservation
Act and the Panchayat (Extension to the
Scheduled Areas) (PESA) Act as well as
guidelines issued by the Ministry; and
(b) the steps being taken for harmonious
interpretation of these laws to resolve the
conflicts on the ground?
World Bank assistance for Rural
Development Projects
†*463. SHRI RANJITSINH
VIJAYSINH MOHITE PATIL: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT
be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Ministry
is facing shortage of funds and hence it is
not able to implement its projects;
(b) whether it is also a fact that the
Ministry is going to take assistance from
the World Bank for its Flagship Scheme,
viz. National Rural Livelihood Mission
(NRLM);
(c) the names of other projects for
which the Ministry is planning to take
assistance from the World Bank; and

134
(d) the amount of loan sought as soft
loan from the World Bank for all its projects
by the Ministry?
Permanent employment under
MGNREGS
*464. SHRI SHADI LAL BATRA: Will
the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has taken any
decision to provide permanent
employment under the Mahatma Gandhi
National Rural Employment Guarantee
Scheme (MGNREGS);
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) if not, the reasons therefor; and
(d) the steps taken by Government in
this regard?
Restrictions on sale of antibiotics
*465. SHRI S. THANGA VELU: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has restricted
the sale of 90 commonly prescribed
antibiotics to put an end to the misuse of
antibiotics;
(b) whether Government has also
restricted sale of 16 medicines to tertiary
care hospitals directly and sale of 74
medicines only on the prescription of
registered medical practitioners;
(c) if so, the details thereof;
(d) whether All India Organisation of
Chemists and Druggists, the apex body of
over 7 lakh licensed medicines sellers, is
against the move as due to an estimated
loss of business worth ` 5000 crore for the
retail medical stores across the country;
and
(e) if so, the details thereof?
Problems faced by patients at AIIMS
due to renovation works
†*466. SHRIMATI MAYA SINGH :
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether six out of twelve Operation
Theatres (OTs) have been kept non-
operational for a long time due to ongoing
renovation works in the main O.T. block at
AIIMS, New Delhi;
(b) if so, by when these closed OTs
would resume functioning and the time-
limit fixed earlier to complete the renovation
works and the revised time-limit now;
(c) whether problems of patients
coming from various parts of the country
have increased due to non-functioning of
these OTs as they are forced to wait
indefinitely for operation; and
(d) the arrangements in place to tackle
day-to-day problems being faced by
patients in AIIMS?
Increase in pension for widows in BPL
category
*467. SHRI PARIMAL NATHWANI:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) the number of widows of BPL
category in the country who get ` 200 per
month as pension under the Government
scheme, State-wise;
(b) whether BPL widows are adequately
aware of the scheme across India;
(c) whether there is any plan to increase
the amount of pension, which is very
meagre at present; and
(d) whether Government has any other
such scheme for BPL widows?
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.

135
Assistance from Japan for PMGSY
projects in Karnataka
*468. DR. VIJAY MALLYA: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether the Ministry has received a
proposal in December, 2009 from the State
Government of Karnataka for financial
assistance under the Japan International
Cooperation Agency in order to cover the
road length of 5000 Km. at an estimated
cost of ` 1982.00 crore under the Pradhan
Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY);
(b) if so, whether the matter has been
considered by the Ministry; and
(c) by when the Ministry would
approve the proposal to enable the State
Government to complete the work?
Implementation of SCSS, 2004 in
banks
*469. SHRI RAJEEV
CHANDRASEKHAR: Will the Minister
of FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) the salient features of the Senior
Citizens Saving Scheme (SCSS), 2004;
(b) whether it has come to the notice of
the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) that some
of the banks do not implement Senior
Citizens Saving Scheme (SCSS), 2004,
particularly in case of retired army
personnel and have denied the facility of
SCSS to some of them in contravention of
the instructions;
(c) if so, the reasons therefor;
(d) the steps being taken by
Government to ensure that such incidents
do not take place in future and
Government's orders are implemented
scrupulously; and
(e) the details of action taken against
such banks?
Assessment of RRBs’ functioning
*470. SHRI DHIRAJ PRASAD SAHU:
Will the Minister of FINANCE be pleased
to state:
(a) whether Government has assessed
the functioning of the Regional Rural Banks
(RRBs) in the country;
(b) if so, the follow-up action taken after
such assessment;
(c) whether credit delivery to rural
masses through RRBs has improved; and
(d) if so, the extent thereof?
Shelter for rural residents
*471. SHRI N.K. SINGH: Will the
Minister of RURAL DEVELOPMENT be
pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
come up with an ambitious scheme for
providing shelter to all rural residents
based on the recommendations of a
committee;
(b) if so, the salient features of the
scheme;
(c) whether Government has since
examined the recommendations of the
committee; and
(d) if so, the details of the
recommendations Government proposes to
accept and implement?
Selective roll back of MGNREGS
*472. SHRI SYED AZEEZ PASHA:
Will the Minister of RURAL
DEVELOPMENT be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government has decided to
roll back the Mahatma Gandhi National
Rural Employment Guarantee Scheme
(MGNREGS) from 600 districts in the
country to just 200;

136
†Original notice of the question received in Hindi.
(b) if so, the reasons therefor;
(c) the criteria to be applied for selecting
any district to become eligible for
MGNREGS;
(d) whether the selection process has
already been completed; and
(e) the names of districts in Andhra
Pradesh which would be ineligible for
MGNREGS for the year 2012-13?
Plantation of trees
*473. SHRI MANGALA KISAN: Will
the Minister of ENVIRONMENT AND
FORESTS be pleased to state the details
of the amount spent for plantation of
trees and the numbers of trees planted
during the last three years in the country,
year-wise, State-wise and district-wise?
Overseas capital investments by
Indians
†*474. SHRI RAMCHANDRA
PRASAD SINGH: Will the Minister of
FINANCE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that the Indian
capital investors are investing their capital
in the world market;
(b) if so, the amount of capital invested
by Indians outside the country in the first
three months of 2009-10, 2010-11 and
2011-12; and
(c) the amount of capital invested,
country-wise and industry-wise?
Shelter for patients and attendants at
AIIMS
†*475. SHRI SHREEGOPAL VYAS:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether Government is aware of the
fact that people coming for treatment at
the most prestigious Government Institute,
AIIMS, have to bide their time on roads
and on footpaths, and patients and their
relatives are compelled to spend a number
of days under the open sky for the sake of
their treatment; and
(b) if so, the efforts being made by
Government to provide shelter to these
patients and their relatives?
Inclusion of Rajiv Aarogyasri under
NRHM
*476. SHRI MOHD. ALI KHAN: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether the State Government of
Andhra Pradesh has requested the Ministry
to include the Rajiv Aarogyasri under
National Rural Health Mission (NRHM)
by bearing some financial expenditure; and
(b) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken so far?
Non-availability  of  essential
medicines in Government
hospitals
*477. SHRI SATISH CHANDRA
MISRA: Will the Minister of HEALTH
AND FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) the details of medicines covered
under the National List of Essential
Medicines;
(b) whether all these medicines are
available at the hospitals run by
Government; and
(c) if not, the reasons for the non-
availability of these essential medicines in
Government run hospitals?

137
NEW DELHI; V . K. AGNIHOTRI,
The 30th August, 2011 Secretary-General.
Bhadra 8, 1933 (Saka)
Rise in cases of depression and
hypertension
*478. SHRI RAJKUMAR DHOOT:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) whether it is a fact that cases of
depression and hypertension, particularly
amongst the youth, are increasing rapidly
in the country;
(b) if so, the details thereof;
(c) whether any study has been
conducted in this regard;
(d) if so, the outcome thereof; and
(e) the steps Government proposes to
take for counselling and treatment of cases of
depression and hypertension in the country?
Role of ASHAs in JSY
*479. SHRI A VINASH PANDE: Will
the Minister of HEALTH AND FAMILY
WELFARE be pleased to state:
(a) the role of ASHAs in achieving the
target of 100 per cent institutional delivery
under the Janani Surksha Yojana (JSY);
(b) the amount of funds allocated under
JSY since its inception in 2005, State-wise;
(c) the number of pregnancy cases
covered by the scheme in the last five
financial years;
(d) whether Government has estimated
the number of cases of unattended
pregnancy; and
(e) if so, the details thereof, State-wise?
Guidelines for using radioactive
equipment in hospitals
*480. DR. K. P. RAMALINGAM:
Will the Minister of HEALTH AND
FAMILY WELFARE be pleased to
state:
(a) whether it is a fact that many
hospitals under the State and Central
Governments neither have any guidelines
nor follow the safety measures, while using
radioactive equipment;
(b) if so, the details thereof and whether
Government has any monitoring
mechanism to ensure that all radioactive
equipment in Government hospitals are
utilized following guidelines and with
safety measures; and
(c) if so, the details thereof and the action
taken by Government in this regard?

I N D E X
(Ministry-wise)
Drinking Water and Sanitation :—
Environment and Forests : 462, 473,
Finance : 469, 470, 474,
Health and Family Welfare : 461, 465, 466, 475, 476, 477, 478, 479,
480,
Heavy Industries and Public Enterprises:—
Petroleum and Natural Gas :—
Rural Development : 463, 464, 467, 468, 471, 472.
138
MGIPMRND—1628RS—30-08-2011.
